eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts and climatological data position 12–13°C as the leading outcomes for Wellington’s daily maximum temperature on August 2. New Zealand’s National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research (NIWA) seasonal outlook indicates near-average temperatures are most likely for the Wellington region through August, consistent with long-term averages of roughly 12°C daytime highs during the Southern Hemisphere winter. Maritime influences, including frequent southerly flows and cloud cover, typically moderate extremes, while short-range model guidance (such as Met Office runs) points to a 12°C peak under stable conditions. Market-implied odds reflect this consensus, with limited upside potential from warmer advection or downside risk from stronger cold fronts. Updated official forecasts from NIWA or MetService in the next 24 hours could refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.

Ensemble spreads remain tight around these values because limited cloud cover and weak mixing favor modest daytime warming rather than extremes. Updated 00 UTC guidance tomorrow morning will refine boundary-layer details ahead of market resolution.
